# libvpx / vpx_enc_fuzzer_vp9

libvpx's own fuzz target `vpx_enc_fuzzer_vp9` ([source](source/vpx_enc_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libvpx (chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx at 5c880e08).

Byte 0 picks keyframe interval, deadline and one of 6 tiny frame sizes; the rest is copied into I420 planes frame by frame (up to 150/300 frames) and encoded with vpx_codec_encode; compressed packets are fwrite()n to /dev/null and never decoded back (no encode->decode check).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libvpx at commit 5c880e08.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- assert(img->bit_depth == 8) in fuzz_vpx_img_read; the image is always allocated as 8-bit VPX_IMG_FMT_I420, so this is trivially true ([line 104](source/vpx_enc_fuzzer.cc#L104)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- vpx_codec_enc_config_default must succeed; called with constant arguments before any input byte is used, so it is input-independent ([line 184](source/vpx_enc_fuzzer.cc#L184)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of the check at line 104 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name it exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies it on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other check.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libvpx` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `vpx_enc_fuzzer_vp9.plain` | 941,688 | `878abedeeaa692494c0c8c58d96b5e2e8025f7214685271fd688ac13ed9097ba` |
| ubsan | `vpx_enc_fuzzer_vp9.ubsan` | 1,266,632 | `dc7432bfe1649ea98d394574a2c5279f555bc663b5c18332edc5c657f36abf1d` |
| asan | `vpx_enc_fuzzer_vp9.asan` | 2,971,288 | `1a4bd8ab876257ec3048a9c0331223fbc17891007fb4b1b6dcb97fc4fde33a86` |
| asan-ubsan | `vpx_enc_fuzzer_vp9.asan-ubsan` | 3,206,168 | `6382743fb3355a8f356329d56dc706bb2ce19f20032cfdba11b6209e9ad73636` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
